chunks: Al-Tawhid, Ma'ani al-Akhbar and Uyun Akhbar al-Ridha: Al-Taliqani, from Ahmad al-Hamdani, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal, from his father who said:

I asked al-Ridha (peace be upon him) about Bismillah. He said: The meaning of the words of the one who says Bismillah is - I mark myself with a mark from the marks of Allah Mighty and Majestic, and that is worshipful servitude. He said: So I said to him: What is the mark? He said: A distinguishing emblem.

key_terms.السِّمَةُ: A mark, sign, or distinguishing emblem
key_terms.الْعُبُودِيَّةُ: Servitude or worshipful submission to God

ai.seo_question: What is the deeper theological meaning of saying Bismillah according to Imam al-Ridha?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him) elucidates that 'Bismillah' signifies the speaker identifying themselves with the divine attribute of servitude (ubudiyyah) through a distinguishing sign (sima). This interpretation shifts the focus from mere invocation to a profound ontological connection, where the believer's identity is marked by their submission to Allah's majesty. Such a nuanced understanding aligns with Shia theological emphasis on the intimate relationship between the Creator and the created, highlighting servitude as the ultimate mark of distinction.

en.ammaar-muslim: [1/1576] al-Tawhid, Ma’ani al-Akhbar and Uyun Akhbar al-Ridha: Al-Taliqani from Ahmad al-Hamdani from Ali b. al-Hasan b. Fadhal from his father (al-Hasan) who said:

I asked al-Ridha عليه السلام about Bismillah. He said: The meaning of the words of the one who says Bismillah is - Asumm (I mark) my self with a Sima (mark) from the marks of Allah Mighty and Majestic, and that (mark) is worshipful servitude. He (al-Hasan) said: So I said to him: What is Sima? He said: A distinguishing emblem
